# 古音叢目

**ID:** KR1j0069
**Custom ID:** ZB1j0064

**Source:** 四庫全書 文淵閣版, V239.2, p241
**Extent:** 1 卷

## Authors / Editors
- 楊愼 (明朝) 撰 1488 - 1559

**Editions:** WYG

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A Míng-period catalogue of Old-Chinese phonological readings, in 5 *juàn*. The first instalment of Yáng Shèn's four-part *gǔyīn* (Old-phonology) project: catalogued by the Sìkù as *Gǔyīn cóngmù* 古音叢目 (5 *juàn*), *Gǔyīn lièyào* 古音獵要 (5 *juàn*), *Gǔyīn yú* 古音餘 (5 *juàn*), *Gǔyīn fùlù* 古音附錄 (1 *juàn*) — together transmitting Yáng's lifelong collection of Old-period rhyme evidence. The Sìkù compilers note that the four works in fact overlap heavily — sharing 13 graphs in *dōng* / *dōng* alone — and were issued sequentially as Yáng accumulated material rather than as a finished single work. Each adopts the structure of Wú Yù's [吳棫](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%B3%E6%A3%AB) *Yùn bǔ* [KR1j0059](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0059): full *Guǎngyùn* rhyme-class arrangement with each entry-graph cross-referenced to its Old-period rhyme partner. Thoroughness of *biǎozhèng* (text-evidence citation) varies: many graphs in the *Gǔyīn cóngmù* are entered with only "*Shī*" or "*Chǔcí*" without specific reference. Where Yáng departs from Old phonology to invent a *xiéyùn* assignment — e.g., putting 龍 into the *jiāng* 江 rhyme to re-rhyme with 封 — the Sìkù *tíyào* points out that 龍 / 紅 / 封 are demonstrably *dōng* / *zhōng* class graphs (citing *Yìshuōguà* commentaries by Yú Fān and Gàn Bǎo, and the *Zhōulǐ Jīnchē* gloss). The *tíyào* concludes Yáng is broader-read than Chén Dì [陳第](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E7%AC%AC) but does not understand Old-phonology root-and-branch — a useful raw collection but unreliable for principled research.

**Abstract**

The *Gǔyīn cóngmù* (with its three companions *Lièyào* / *Yú* / *Fùlù*) is a Míng-period collection of Old-Chinese phonological evidence — datable broadly to Yáng Shèn's mature career (c. 1530s–1559) and probably issued piecemeal during his exile in Yúnnán. Conceptually still within the *xiéyùn* paradigm of Wú Yù's [吳棫](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%B3%E6%A3%AB) *Yùn bǔ* — i.e., reading Old-phonology as ad-hoc shifts from a Sòng-rhyme base — and therefore, for the Sìkù compilers, methodologically inferior to Chén Dì's [陳第](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E7%AC%AC) *Máo Shī gǔyīn kǎo* [KR1j0072](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0072) (1606) and Gù Yánwǔ's [顧炎武](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A1%A7%E7%82%8E%E6%AD%A6) later *Yīnlùn* [KR1j0078](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0078) (1667). The work is significant chiefly as an evidence-gathering exercise — Yáng's reading-range across pre-Qín texts is broad — that later Qīng *gǔyīnxué* (Gù, Jiāng Yǒng [江永](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B1%9F%E6%B0%B8), Duàn Yùcái) drew on selectively. Date bracket follows Yáng Shèn's lifedates 1488–1559.
